plan: A bhajan lit as one lamp becoming a congregation and going out again: the room rests near-dark on a single saffron flame, turns white the instant the harmony goes D-minor to D-major at bar 15, splits into leader and responders through the call-and-response at bars 31-38, burns brightest across bars 45-48 where the recording itself is loudest, and then empties - the void at bar 54 held on one lamp for one voice, the octave lift at bar 58 where the music finally goes major and the light rises and stays, and three bars of real darkness to finish.

states.why: The rig is at true zero until bar 1 - the show starts from black, not from a bed. Bars 1-2 are 36-37% loud with lead-vocal and cello alone: one flame on the left pair, par_15 and par_22 genuinely off.

Bar 2 is where vocal and bass join the lead (5 onsets against 3). The flame steps inward and up a little - the resting look changes on the bar line rather than holding one dim state across the whole opening.

Bar 3 is the song's quietest bar (25%, french-horn) and bar 4 is percussion and congas at 43% with 7 hits - moment 0, the drums thickening. The flame crosses to the right pair, so by bar 5 every lamp has been alone at least once. Extended to bar 5: the resting layer had a 1.4s hole here and the rig went to true black in the middle of a verse, with lead-vocal and cello still playing. A hole in the base is not a blackout; it is nothing being asked for.

Moment 1 (intensity 1.00) is synth and back-vocal entering at bar 5 beat 3 - and the two beats before it have no state at all, so the room is fully dark when they arrive. The room then opens from two lamps to four and turns indigo; drone gives every lamp its own breathing phase, so four lamps widen without the rig reading as one body.

Moment 2: the tempo settles from 89 to 119 bpm at bar 7 and loudness jumps to 59%, the loudest bars of the intro (tuba, wind, brass). First bed of the show that actually travels, and the brightest thing so far - which is what gives moment 3's spotlight two bars later something to fall from.
Bars 9-10 sit under the isolate; this is the ember it returns to if anything slips at the seam.

Bars 11-13 are violin, timpani and viola over a D-minor/A-minor cycle - moving but not loud (43-55%). Indigo keeps the minor mode; par_1 and par_22 are held by the accent binding, so this bed shows on the inner pair only and the rig is genuinely split.

The hinge of the first half: D:min becomes D at 33.80s, drum hits jump 0 to 12 in a bar, and guitar, strings and acoustic-guitar all enter. Marigold on the major chord, and a bed where every beat lands hard from a low floor - what a dholak entering actually sounds like. Pulled down to almost nothing for the build: a wave is one lamp lit against three dark ones, and it cannot be seen at all over a lit bed. The room is the wave here, not a bed with a wave on top.

Bar 18 is double-bass, bass and guitar - the low end takes over from the drum entry. The bump starts travelling across the lamps again, same marigold, so the bed follows who is leading rather than holding four bars of one look. Pulled down to almost nothing for the build: a wave is one lamp lit against three dark ones, and it cannot be seen at all over a lit bed. The room is the wave here, not a bed with a wave on top.

Bars 19-21 are 63/61/68% - the instrumental's own peak, and the loudest thing so far. First time every beat hits and the downbeat flashes white. Ends at bar 22 and nothing replaces it. Pulled down to almost nothing for the build: a wave is one lamp lit against three dark ones, and it cannot be seen at all over a lit bed. The room is the wave here, not a bed with a wave on top.

Bar 22 is the producer's own dropout (39%, ukulele and sitar) and gets no state - the rig empties to a single lamp, par_15, still breathing with the voice on the binding. Bar 23 is where the chorus really lands (73%, kick and electric-guitar in). Marigold against rose: the congregation. Floor lifted from 0.34 to 0.62: the eight bars of build before this ran at 0.75 with the row wide open, and the payoff was landing at 0.45 with the lamps nearly level. A drop that is dimmer than its own build reads as the lights giving up exactly where the song does not.

Bar 30 dips to 48% between bars at 74% and 82% - one of only two places this 33-second section can breathe. The room halves rather than dimming: the inner pair goes out and the two edge lamps carry the vocal line alone.

Bars 31-34 are where lead-vocal and back-vocal actually trade (correlation -0.75 measured over exactly this span; back-vocal does not exist before bar 31). A travelling bump per beat is the sway of a kirtan, and the trades ride on top of it. Floor 0.50: enough that the drop at bar 31 beats its build, not so much that the show peaks here -- the band's heaviest stretch is forty seconds later and the room should be biggest there.

Bars 35-37 are the loudest of the whole chorus (87/84/85%). The phrase escalates into drive for its last three bars rather than repeating - a second chorus that sounds bigger should look bigger, and every beat now hits. Floor lifted from 0.42 to 0.72: the eight bars of build before this ran at 0.75 with the row wide open, and the payoff was landing at 0.45 with the lamps nearly level. A drop that is dimmer than its own build reads as the lights giving up exactly where the song does not.

Section 3 is the same chorus a third time, so it gets the same bed in a different pair of colours - rose against indigo, the two coldest things in the palette, because back-vocal has taken over from the lead here (back-vocal mean 0.63, lead-vocal 0.08). Floor 0.38 -> 0.70: this span carries the third and hardest drop at 83.8s, and it was landing at 0.49 against a build of 0.65. The last drop in the song was the smallest thing in the show.

Bars 43-46 are 89/88/85/90% with toms and drums leading, and the recording's loudest five seconds centre at 97.0s. The floor comes up to 0.60 - the highest resting level anywhere in the show. This is where the rig stops breathing and starts burning.

No from_bar, so this starts at the section boundary (97.29s) rather than at bar 47 - the half second between them is dead centre of the song's loudest five-second window and must not be dark. Bar 47 is the single loudest bar of the song at 92%, so it keeps the same 0.60 floor.

The harmony turns to G:min at 101.4s and bar 51 is woodwind, harmonica and flute - the reed break. Still 83-84% loud, so not a retreat: a hard hit on every beat from a low floor, which is the same energy with completely different texture, and it gives bar 53's collapse something to fall from. Floor lifted to 0.74: this is where the band is heaviest in the whole song -- six families at once -- and it was sitting on 0.20, so the show was peaking thirty-five seconds away from the music. Changed from breakdown to drive: breakdown hits from a very low floor by design, and this is the loudest stretch of the record -- the four hardest kicks in the song are inside it. It was making the biggest part of the music the dimmest part of the show.
Bar 53 is 37% loud with zero drum hits. Back to the saffron flame the show opened on, now on the two edge lamps - par_15 belongs to the strings binding for the whole outro.

Bar 54 deliberately has NO state - the void (12% loud, the quietest instant in the song at 113.0s). Bar 55 is where bass and acoustic-guitar come back; a plain held indigo fill at the level the hush four beats later falls FROM, so that exit reads as a pure fall and not a bump followed by one.
Moment 13 took the lead-vocal, tambourine and vocal out; bar 56 is harp, banjo and tambourine at 32%. Two lamps at the edges, the middle of the room empty.
Strings and double-bass return at bar 57 (54%) and the outro starts moving again. Still indigo - the harmony is D:min into D:7, not resolved yet.

The chord goes to D major at 120.00s, at the same instant as the octave shift. The bed turns marigold underneath the lift so that when the lift's span ends the room stays warm rather than snapping back to night.

Bar 60 is the outro's summit: lead-vocal and vocal re-enter, strings 0.97, cello 1.00, dobro 1.00. The only place in the outro every beat hits, and a floor high enough that the swell blooming out of it does not leave a hole. Ends at bar 62, so the last half-bar of the section is already going dark.

Every one of the 39 lanes measures 0.00 in this section. One ember for a second and a half, then no state at all to the end of the file - the show finishes in real darkness, not in a bed held over silence.

bindings.why: This section's whole story is the drums arriving: 3, 1, 0, 0 hits in bars 11-14, then 11-13 hits a bar from bar 15 on. Bound to the real onsets rather than the grid, on par_15 alone with rest 0 - so that lamp does not exist until the drums do, while the other three carry the state. Threshold 0.14 measured to leave it dark about 60% of the section.

Across the 33-second chorus the voice is the only thing continuously present (vocal median 0.32, carrying 72.5% of the span) - and in a kirtan the room drives while one person sings. par_15 breathes with the singer for the whole section and drops to black between phrases; response 2.4 is what makes it drop rather than hover.

Strings are the one lane that genuinely carries the outro - mean 0.65 and present 81.5% of 113-128s. One lamp (par_15) breathes with the string line for the whole outro and goes fully out between phrases; the other three stay on the cue list. response 2.2 is what makes it drop to black between phrases instead of hovering.

gestures.why: Moment 0: the drums thicken into something - bar 4 jumps to 7 onsets from 1 in bar 3. A single saffron tap on the inner pair, which the state has left dark. Small, because the moment is intensity 0.235.

Moment 1, intensity 1.00: synth and back-vocal enter. The two lamps that have been at zero since the first bar snap on. A stab and not an impact because the bar is only 41% loud - the event is big for this point in the song, not big for the song.

Moment 2 is a real tempo change, 89.3 to 118.8 bpm - a ratio of 1.33, which is exactly what the lighting rate is multiplied by. The one place in the song a rate gesture is literally true. Colour named explicitly: gear paints the whole row and falls back to a warm default, which was the only non-house colour left in the show.

One beat of black on the last beat of bar 8, so moment 3's spotlight is found rather than switched to. Same grammar as the hole before bar 15, at a fraction of the scale - one beat instead of three, a single lamp instead of the whole rig - so the show has a vocabulary rather than a habit.
Moment 3 (0.93): everything drops back behind lead-vocal. One lamp lit, three at true black, the head turned to face it. Held two bars because the spotlight is a passage, not a hit.
First of three stacked beats of black before the major chord at bar 15. Bar 14 is 26% loud with zero drum hits - the emptiest bar of the first half, and the producer has already done most of this.
Second beat of the hole. Moment 4's pause reads at 33.0s, inside this.
Third beat, abutting bar 15 beat 1 so the white lands out of nothing. Stacked single beats rather than one long blackout because that is what holds a real hole on this rig.

D:min becomes D at 33.80s, drum hits go 0 to 12, guitar and strings and acoustic-guitar all enter on the same downbeat. The first of the show's white arrivals. Nothing else starts on this anchor - a tier-one hit needs its downbeat to itself or it gets cancelled.

Bar 15, beats 1 and 2: the whole row blazes. This is the half of the bar that carries the weight, and it is what the run in the second half falls out of -- a single lamp half a second after the room was full reads far harder than the same lamp in a room that was already dark. Level 0.55, escalating bar by bar so eight repeats of one figure still build.

Beat 3: the row collapses to ONE lamp and it runs RIGHT TO LEFT across all four in a single beat -- about 125 milliseconds a lamp. Everything else is at zero, so there is one light in the room and it is moving. per_beat is crossings per beat now, so one means the light crosses the whole row once in the beat -- and it means the same thing on four lamps or sixteen.

Beat 4: and straight back the other way, LEFT TO RIGHT. The turn inside the bar is what makes the room rock rather than just flicker. per_beat is crossings per beat now, so one means the light crosses the whole row once in the beat -- and it means the same thing on four lamps or sixteen.

THE DROP. Two beats of NOTHING after eight bars of the row running -- the room has been moving without pause and then stops dead. This is the single biggest moment in the show and it has to land in an empty room.

The wave carries straight through the drop rather than stopping at it. The build ends with one lamp lit against three dark ones, which is a huge picture; if the drop settles into an even bed it reads as smaller than the run-up that led to it. So the row keeps crossing, a lamp per quarter beat, off a small floor. per_beat is crossings per beat now, so one means the light crosses the whole row once in the beat -- and it means the same thing on four lamps or sixteen.

Moment 6, intensity 1.00: the climax, the whole band at full strength with six instrument families at once. The fullest passage of the song gets the white flash; the loudest passage gets something else, twenty seconds later.

The harmony turns to C at 57.87s and bar 27 is the tambourine's loudest bar (78%). A partial hit on the inner pair - different effect, different extent and different colour from the impact three bars earlier, so two neighbouring cues do not read as one habit.
One beat of nothing before the drums come back full at bar 31.
Bar 31 lands. The build was kept cold on purpose so this is the first white the room sees.

The call and response is real and it lives here: lead-vocal against back-vocal correlates -0.75 over bars 31-39, and back-vocal does not exist before bar 31. Saffron left hands to rose right - the leader calls and the room answers. Trade is the only effect on this rig that is both full-rig and genuinely per-lamp. Contrast raised: the sections after the drop now sit on a high floor, and a bump cannot be seen against a bright bed unless it starts from near nothing.

Moment 7: lead-vocal enters. The handoff is placed on the entrance itself rather than on the bar line. Contrast raised: the sections after the drop now sit on a high floor, and a bump cannot be seen against a bright bed unless it starts from near nothing.

Third exchange, bars 35-37 being the loudest of the chorus (87/84/85%). Contrast raised: the sections after the drop now sit on a high floor, and a bump cannot be seen against a bright bed unless it starts from near nothing.

Fourth and last exchange, colours reversed so the answer comes back the other way before the section drops out. Contrast raised: the sections after the drop now sit on a high floor, and a bump cannot be seen against a bright bed unless it starts from near nothing.

Bar 38 dips to 50% between bars at 86% and gets no state - a second hole. Rather than fill it, put white flickers in it that accelerate into a hardware-strobe burst on the last beat, and let bar 39 arrive out of that. Anticipation is dark between pops, so the hole survives.
One beat of nothing before bar 40, the hardest span in the song.
Corner-to-corner head snaps over the drive while toms and drums take the front of the mix. Head only - it costs the pars nothing at the loudest point of the show.

Moment 9, intensity 1.00, and the loudest half-second in the recording (92.5s). Half a second of hardware strobe - sharper than any framed flash, and deliberately a different gesture from the two impacts so the biggest three events of the show are three different things.

The recording's loudest five-second window centres at 97.00s, not at the 92.5s headline. This swell starts at 93.76s and crests at 96.99s, so the show's brightest sustained passage sits exactly on the song's. Bars 45-49 are left clear of every other gesture because a short cue placed inside a long one replaces it rather than layering over it.

Moment 11: the track strips back. A controlled pull-back that empties the rig from the edges inward across the section boundary and lands exactly at bar 54, the void. Six beats, so it is still falling when the section changes - holds at the floor rather than returning, because the band does not come back.

The one honest isolate in the song. At 112.0-112.75s lead-vocal reads 0.40 and vocal 0.28 with all 37 other lanes between 0.00 and 0.02 - a single voice alone. One saffron lamp, three at true black, and not the lamp that has been breathing with the strings all outro.
Moment 12 (0.85): 113.0s is the quietest instant in the whole song, loudness 0.022. The flame goes out. Darkness is the strongest gesture available and this is the place to spend it.

Moment 13, intensity 1.00: lead-vocal, tambourine and vocal all drop out at 115.29s - confirmed in the lanes, all three go from 0.4-0.6 to 0.00 within two windows. The room quiets with them and settles into bar 56's two edge lamps.
Strings and double-bass rebuild through bar 57 with the pars low; the head carries the motion on its own until the lift takes it.

Moment 14, intensity 1.00, and the emotional resolution of the whole piece: the music moves up an octave at 120.29s and the chord turns to D major at 120.00s after two minutes of D minor. Seven beats, so the rise runs right up to bar 60 beat 1 and hands straight to the swell - it arrives and stays arrived, with no sag back to the bed. Only +0.34 though: bar 58 is 42% loud against bar 47's 92%, and a register shift is an emotional event, not a loud one. It must not out-shine the peak.

Moment 15, intensity 1.00: lead-vocal and vocal return at 123.77s and strings, cello and dobro all peak within the next second (0.97, 1.00, 1.00). The crest lands at 124.4s on that spike and is gone again in two - a bloom, not a plateau, so the outro stays the outro. Marigold, not white: this is warmth arriving, not a hit.

Moment 16: the beat drops away at 126.71s. Half a second of nothing, and then the show is already in its last dark bar. A small gesture for a 0.18 moment - most moments in this song get nothing at all.

THE DROP. Two beats of absolute black before it, then the entire rig at FULL WHITE and held, not a flash that decays inside a tenth of a second. The build spends the whole bar before this at full glare and then vanishes; this is what the room comes back as.

Two beats of nothing before the loudest kick in the song. Everything stops -- and this is the one place in the record where the whole band is already at full, so the hole is the loudest thing in the room.

THE LOUDEST KICK IN THE SONG at 102.76s -- full strength in the kick lane, the top of four consecutive bars that hold the four hardest hits on the record. Whole rig, full white, held for three beats. This is the peak of the show and it is placed on the hit rather than on a bar line.

A genuine 200ms hole at 64.2s: the band falls to under half its own level right here, just before the drums come back full. Black for exactly as long as the hole, so the room breathes with the track instead of over it.
The same thing at 80.1s, 250ms, on the approach to the next drop.
